nodes.description: The JAK1/2 inhibitor baricitinib was given in an open-label expanded-access study of 35 patients with genetically confirmed Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome. The interferon signature fell, symptom diaries improved and many children gained new developmental milestones. The cohort mixed AGS genotypes and the cached report does not give results by gene, so the evidence applies to AGS7 only as part of AGS.

nodes.description: The JAK1/2 inhibitor ruxolitinib, which blocks signaling from the type I interferon receptor, has been given off label to three patients in two reports. In a child with SMS1, psoriasis cleared and the interferon signature normalized within days, and weakness, osteopenia and growth improved. Two brothers with AGS7 presenting as spastic paraplegia had a significant fall in the interferon signature, better quality of life, and maintained or slightly improved motor function.
